Section 4B: Top 3 Institutional Pre-Print Debates & Analyst Call Focus Questions
SELL-SIDE PREVIEW AUDIT
Debate 1: AI Search Disruption vs. Search Monetization Moat — Are AI Overviews Cannibalizing Queries?

Bull vs. Bear Institutional Framing: Bulls argue Google's AI Overviews have increased overall query volume, boosted user satisfaction, and unlocked higher click-through rates on high-intent commercial shopping queries. Bears contend that conversational answer engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude) are eroding Google's traditional 90%+ global search market share, especially for technical, programming, and product research queries, threatening high-margin ad impressions.

Analyst Focus Question: 'Can management share specific metrics on query growth, cost-per-query reductions with Gemini Flash, and monetization rates for commercial queries featuring AI Overviews compared to traditional text ad links?'

Debate 2: Google Cloud AI Growth & Custom TPU Margins — Is GCP Closing the Gap on AWS and Azure?

Bull vs. Bear Institutional Framing: Bulls highlight that Google Cloud is growing faster than Azure and AWS (+32% YoY in Q2), fueled by unique hardware cost advantages from custom Trillium TPUs that allow enterprise customers to train and serve multimodal models at 40-50% lower cost than Nvidia H100/H200 clusters. Bears argue that enterprise IT spending remains selective, and that cloud infrastructure migrations could slow if enterprise AI pilot projects fail to reach production scale.

Analyst Focus Question: 'What percentage of Google Cloud customers are now utilizing Gemini API or custom TPU compute, and how is the pipeline for multi-year enterprise commitments trending into 2027?'

Debate 3: CapEx Escalation vs. Free Cash Flow Squeeze — When Does Free Cash Flow Re-expand?

Bull vs. Bear Institutional Framing: Bulls emphasize that Alphabet generated $39.07B in operating cash flow in Q2 alone, and that heavy CapEx ($44.92B) is building permanent competitive infrastructure that competitors without multi-trillion dollar balance sheets cannot match. Bears note that True FCF turned negative (-$13.81B post-SBC) in Q2, warning that sustained $160B+ annual CapEx could constrain share buybacks and dividend growth if AI monetization lags.

Analyst Focus Question: 'With Q2 CapEx reaching $44.9B, what is the expected multi-year trajectory for capital intensity, and when does management anticipate CapEx as a percentage of revenue normalizing back toward historical 12-15% levels?'
